claims.reason: rememberRetryableTurnFailure runs after queue.push but before bridgeToResponsesSSE processes the terminal event; cancellation aborts and closes the iterator without revoking the stored handoff, while later exact source-hash guards can still accept it as a successor.

The streaming queue is limited to 10000 objects, but the 32 MiB event-byte budget is skipped for streaming and individual AdapterEvent payloads are not bounded, so retained memory is not byte-bounded.

The report's literal unbounded-count wording is narrowed because AsyncEventQueue caps buffered count at 10000; the actionable defect remains: deliverEvent lacks an abort guard and can retain late post-cancel payloads up to that cap without a byte budget.

roots.title: Retry handoff survives cancellation before streamed terminal delivery
roots.trigger: A retryable 503 error is queued, then the HTTP stream is cancelled before bridgeToResponsesSSE processes and emits response.failed; the stored handoff remains available to a later exact-source successor.
roots.fix: Create the retry handoff only from the bridge's processed terminal-event boundary and revoke any pending handoff when request cancellation wins before that boundary.

roots.title: Streaming adapter queue lacks cancellation and byte bounds
roots.trigger: A slow or cancelled streaming client leaves a non-cooperating adapter callback delivering large AdapterEvent objects; the callback lacks an abort guard and the streaming queue enforces count only, retaining up to 10000 objects with unrestricted payload bytes.
roots.fix: Return immediately from delivery after request abort, close or fail the queue through the cancellation owner, and enforce a streaming byte budget alongside the existing event-count limit.
